errors.text: The hypothesis substitutes a quinary CoCrFeNiMn polycrystalline creep alloy for the quaternary equiatomic FeNiCrMn FCC single crystal.
It replaces high-rate uniaxial molecular-dynamics tension at 10–600 K and 10^8–10^10 s^-1 with experimental creep at 500–600 °C and 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1.
It attributes yielding to diffusion-controlled dislocation climb rather than vacancy-assisted nucleation and glide of Shockley partial dislocations producing stacking faults.

The cited creep evidence does not establish strain-rate-insensitive yield strength; stress exponents and creep activation energies describe steady-state creep kinetics, not the rate dependence of initial yielding.
The falsification experiment distinguishes glide from climb, not dislocation glide from an FCC-to-BCC or other bulk phase transformation as requested.
The proposed baseline incorrectly asserts strong room-temperature yield-rate sensitivity, contrary to the target result of negligible yield-strength sensitivity over 10^8–10^10 s^-1.
